# ANOVA factorial repeated

```{r rmfact-anova-factorial-repeated, echo=FALSE}
rm(list=ls())
source("../../_setup.R")
```

## Factorial repeated measures ANOVA {.section}

The factorial repeated measures ANOVA analyses the variance of the model while reducing the error by the within person variance.

* 1 dependent/outcome variable
* 2 or more independent/predictor variable
    * 2 or more levels
* All with same subjects

## Assumptions

Same as one-way repeated measures ANOVA

## Example {.smaller}

<small>

In this example we will again look at the amount of accidents in a car driving simulator while subjects were given varying doses of speed and alcohol. But this time we let participants partake in all conditions. Every week subjects returned for a different experimental condition.

* Dependent variable
    * Accidents
* Independent variables
    * Speed
        * None
        * Some
        * Much
    * Alcohol
        * None
        * Some
        * Much
        
</small>
        
## {.smaller}

Every participant is measured in every cell of the design

person | 1_1 | 1_2 | 1_3 | 2_1 | 2_2 | 2_3 | 3_1 | 3_2 | 3_3
-------|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|----
1      | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓
2      | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓
3      | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓
⋮      | ⋮ | ⋮ | ⋮ | ⋮ | ⋮ | ⋮ | ⋮ | ⋮ | ⋮
20     | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓

## Data {.smaller .scrollable}

[Data (.csv)](https://johnnydoorn.github.io/teaching-statistics/datasets/RM_ANOVA_AlcoholSpeedTime.csv)

```{r rmfact-data, echo=FALSE}
data <- read.csv(file = datasetsPath("RM_ANOVA_AlcoholSpeedTime.csv"), header = T)

data <- data[, -2]

ssrTable(data, rownames = FALSE)
```

## Balanced by design {.smaller}

```{r rmfact-balanced-cells, echo=FALSE}
# Participants with an observation in each alcohol x speed cell, counted from the data
# above (RM ANOVA only uses participants with all observations).
cellCols <- grep("_alc_", names(data), value = TRUE)
counts <- matrix(colSums(!is.na(data[, cellCols])), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
knitr::kable(data.frame(`Alcohol / speed` = c("none", "some", "much"),
                        none = counts[, 1], some = counts[, 2], much = counts[, 3],
                        check.names = FALSE), align = "lccc")
```

- RM ANOVA only uses participants with all observations
- So every cell holds the same people, always balanced
    - Between-subjects groups (mixed design) can still differ in size
- Balanced, so alcohol and speed are uncorrelated
